newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-NZ PULL OFF THRILLING WIN VS ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NZ PULL OFF THRILLING WIN VS ENGLAND.

text.p: New Zealand pulled off a thrilling nine-run win against England in the fourth one-day cricket international at Eden Park on Sunday to keep their five-match series alive.
New Zealand had been dismissed for a paltry 153 in their innings of a match reduced by rain to 43 overs a side.
But they bowled and fielded superbly, at one stage having England at 41 for four, to pull off the improbable victory.
Fast bowlers Heath Davis and Geoff Allott took two wickets apiece, while old hand Gavin Larsen was at his miserly best, snaring three for just 20 runs off 8.3 overs.
New Zealand had to win this match to have any chance of squaring the series after England won the first two matches and then drew the third in Napier last Wednesday.
Davis let the tourists know New Zealand meant business when he broke opener Nick Knight's left index finger with the first ball of the innings, forcing Knight to retire hurt.
Alec Stewart and Craig White added 50 for the fifth wicket but England struggled against a tight bowling attack and had slumped to 113 for six by the 36th over.
When Robert Croft was run out for 20, Darren Gough caught and bowled next ball and Andrew Caddick bowled in the same over from Larsen, England's innings seemed finished.
But Knight came out to bat as last man with his finger heavily strapped, wearing one batting glove and holding the bat with one hand.
He survived one ball and stayed while Chris Silverwood hit out with some success, raising England's hopes.

England needed 14 from the last two overs when Silverwood smashed Larsen down the ground and Allott took a spectacular catch on the boundary to prohibit a certain six and end the match, with England still nine runs in arrears.
The final game of the five-match series is in Wellington on Tuesday.
